advice: Stop and think before you execute.  Everything from the Dean Witter merger to buying subprime asset shops right before the bubble burst was a disaster.
pros: Decent dase salary.  I enjoyed working with my colleagues very much.
cons: Underperformance is a big problem.  The company became a Frankensteins monster of a bank.  For a long time it couldn't decide which it wanted to be, either a retail oriented firm or the IB of old.

summary: Surrounded and lead by very qualified individuals which makes you feel proud to be part to be part of the firm.
pros: Senior management are very intelligent personnel. Portfolio managers are almost like scientist rather than businessmen. People are approachable and very willing to educate. Sharing of information is emphasized.
cons: As is expected from such a firm, it is very high pressured. And because of MS' position in the field, whatever it does is highly scrutinizes which is noticeable at the work place.

summary: Review of Citi Smith Barney (prior to merger with Morgan Stanley)
advice: Overall, I think management is taking the right approach to changing the corporate structure.
pros: I was an employee of Citi Smith Barney from 2007 - 2010.  The company was willing to invest in growing advisors and did their best to provide them with additional support.
cons: Even back in 2007, it was clear that the company was focusing on their million dollar producers.  Those that didn't appear to have the growth potentional were encouraged to consolidate.

summary: Smart people, pleasant culture, not great pay
advice: Keep the culture, it's very good. Work on improving salaries.
pros: Morgan Stanley is quite strong technically. I work in IT, and I'm quite impressed with the technical sophistication of the shop. The culture is very pleasant too. Not the cut-throat competitive atmosphere I feared when I first started working at the firm.
cons: I think they need to make an effort to be a bit more competitive salary-wise. Many talented people leave due to relatively low pay for Wall Street.

summary: Used to be a great firm, but is slowly headed in the wrong direction
pros: very smart people, good culture, very strong brand, anyone will take your call because you are Morgan Stanley, in the middle of interesting deals so you get to see a lot of action
cons: deferred comp getting crazier and crazier, balance sheet not big enough to compete with the big banks, funding costs not competitive for lending or derivatives, and cutting back on sales and trading

summary: Ok, but follow the sun means fragmented team
advice: I think you're doing a good job to be honest.
pros: salary, name/reputation, lots of training provided
cons: phone conference calls sounds fun, but they're quite dry, and get old quickly, especially at 9pm every night.  follow the sun means that you may have limited opportunities to chat to team mates in different time zones, and you cant just change your working hours to synchronize with them (unless you want to work 24 hours a day of course...)

summary: Great and Highly Professional Culture Given the Intensity of Work
advice: Focus on giving more feedback to employees so they know what to expect when it comes to bonus time.
pros: Morgan Stanley is a great firm and has a leading reputation.  The pros (and, in some ways, cons) include the intensity of work, high quality of outputs, exceptional brand, great culture, and high level of professionalism.
cons: On the flipside, the cons include the high level of intensity, very long hours, and lack of sufficient visibility around bonuses.

summary: They take care of you and will go out of their way to make sure you're happy
pros:
Flexible with work from home arrangements
Good work-life-balance
Reasonable perks, such as:
   - Gym membership subsidies
   - Discounts for goods
   - Free/Reduced Museum Entry fees
   - Occasional access to some "members only" events in the City
cons:
Lower total comp packages than comparable firms
Senior management can be opaque at times; saying one thing but then having to have other management staff have to manage expectations

summary: Rudderless ship a drift and horrible culture to boot
advice: Only way to grow firm and gain necessary control is to fire PM's, hire a CIO and look for some experienced asset management leaders.
pros: Scale, smart fellow employees and good location in NYC
cons: PM's are unchecked and senior management has no idea how to run asset management company.  Compliance, investment in IT and people, compliance, risk and culture is not in the even part of the discussion.  Believe they are a boutique IM firm, but offer mediocre at best value and performance and most of business is intermediary although they lead you to believe they are institutional.  goes to show how little senior management actually knows about business.

summary: Very smart people, competitive and political environment
advice: Create system and rewards for entrepreneurial activity within the firm.  Assess gender discrimination in salaries.
pros: Smart people, good benefits.  Good horizontal mobility.  They take good care of you when you travel.
cons: Gender discrimination against women - I was paid $100k less then my male counterpart for same exact job.  Regulatory environment killed all sense of entrepreneurship.

advice: management is very straight forward and honest from my experience.  thats nice.
pros: respectable company to work for, seems like some departments may be nice to work in.  they are open to letting you move within the company without your manager sand bagging you to keep you.
cons: on the service side of things you gain more and more responsibility and levels of expertise with no increase in pay.  cant say that i've ever seen a company consider a move into a management position as lateral before.

summary: Spent 4 months interning with MSSB in Atlanta
pros: High standard;  steep learning curve and super nice people; always help you when you confront a problem or even run into trouble in your life. Learned a lot about basic finance knowledge through the internship.
cons: sometimes could be overly intensive; people's instruction could be vague and they expect you to figure it out yourself, which sometimes is basically impossible (for example, they would assume you already familiar with lots of jargon and concepts which can not be looked up online

pros: Great place to start and learn the business.  Paid training.
cons:
Once your business is established you are significantly better off leaving and going independent.  Payouts don't only jump from 40-45% to 90%+, but there is compensation that isn't credited to your grid that makes the pay closer to 3 to 4 times more, not just double.

All the resources you have at MS is available on the independent channel and more.  You have a harder time figuring out what to do than finding something at all.

summary: Advisory center needs to understand direction and alignment
advice: Lose the ego and open your eyes to what your advisors need. Stop focusing on projects that are failing and learn when to shut it down. Treat your people better, they are what make everything happen act like it.
pros: Flexible work schedule, colleagues are good people.
cons: Leadership has no clue of the culture in south Jordan and they do not know what their plan is moving forward, too much shooting from the hip. Lack of communication between managers and advisors.

advice: Management has been very supportive towards career movements and they should keep it up. Perhaps promoting good staff for horizontal movement if the good staff is unable to be promoted due to quota full. This would help retain their good staff.
pros:
Promotes work life balance and professionalism.
Very nice colleagues to work with. Opportunity to cross career across the globe.
cons: Promote better remuneration package, hiring on contractual basis should be eliminated as i believe everyone should have equal opportunities as perm staff after finishing probation period.

advice: Listen to the field and employees more, try to garner additional perspective and utilize individuals closer to clients and revenue to gain realtime perspective.
pros: Large company, stable, big balance sheet.  Big budget to reinvest in technology and product. Have the ability to provide a customer service and solutions that are first rate.
cons: Difficult to have a voice or provide feedback.  Information flows one way, down hill with zero interest in garnering any other perspective. Constantly have to lobby for pay, and justify your compensation.

pros: Tons of opportunities for career advancement and professional growth. Intelligent teams of people, some of the best, so you can easily find your niche and become an expert in the area of choice. The culture of giving back to communities/charities is another plus.
cons: Work/Life balance can be challenging. It is a big bank, so they are still traditional in some ways. While other companies have taken advantage of technology, working at MS still requires a lot of face-time and in many cases, long hours.

pros:
Supports in career development.
Great place to learn nitty gritty of work assigned to you.
cons: There are cons in every entity. Bias exists everywhere because this depends on the manager. in short, not everyone is the same. A corporation is not responsible as such but managers are. You will find few managers who exceptionally perform and help people under them to perform in similar manner and vice versa.  Personally have not met with negativity and have loved to work at Morgan Stanley.

advice: More organization for project management - need to hold people accountable. Hire based on communication skills - not all technical. Poor presenters can give team a bad look to stakeholders
pros: Challenging work (a lot different than line operations), senior management exposure, true agile environment, collaborative coworkers and able to add value even as a junior employee
cons: A lot of politics and key stakeholders can be rude. Can feel micromanaged by stakeholders demanding transparency.  Seem to be interviewing non stop and have very low retention

summary: PWM is stuck between a rock and a hard place.
advice: I wouldn't know where to begin.....On the PWM side Morgan Stanley wants to be a "Modern Wealth Management"  firm but they have to many legacy advisers and practices to accomplish that, IMO. Tough to manage quarterly earnings and keep AUM. To be fair to Mr. Gorman he has a thankless job.
pros: Vast array of resources. operational support via telephone is helpful.
cons: No real structure or training along with no operation support.  Lots of videos but those aren't super helpful.

summary: Good Place to work - room for improvement
advice: The Sr Management is great and have turned the business around after all the turmoil few years back.
pros:
Morgan Stanley is a Great company to work for It's a Leading Investment Bank on Wall St. 

The compensation is fairly good but the variance between good & bad performer is not very high & would like to see that.

Most co-workers are smart & great to work with.
cons: No synergy bertween different business units. Mobility is a challenge as well.

summary: My career starting place and it brought me tons of opportunities from other big companies.
advice: The internship opportunities are the most wonderful ones for college students and I really appreciated it, would like to recommend it to all my college classmates.
pros: Great group to work with, the environment is so friendly and I love the group, everyone is very helpful .
cons: The department is not what I'm looking for for my future career since I'm technical person and would like to get into IT department.

summary: Great place to work after college or MBA
advice: Invest more in your people and do not follow the typical wall street trend of over hiring and over firing.
pros: MS is a great platform to start your career. The brand name within the finance world is second only to GS and will open plenty of doors in the future.
cons: The atmosphere can be very political just like any other investment bank. In addition, management tends to be very short-sighted (i.e. what have you done for me lately).

advice: Professionals become financial advisors to run their own business.   Management doesn't seem to understand that after just a few years, the opportunity to leave the firm is great.  Treat your people well.
pros: The firm has tremendous resources, although due to missed opportunities to properly train it's people the firm missed opportunities to leverage it's strengths.
cons: The merger of Morgan Stanley and Smith Barney has created unrest and disorganization.  Management fails to communicate effectively... And ultimately clients burden that disconnection.

advice: Look closely at the junior and midlevel talent at the firm and consider the quality of the development and training in place. They are the future of Wall Street and of Morgan Stanley.
pros: Respected Institution that provides a difficult interview process to gain admittance to the analyst or associate programs. Worth the headache to get into the sales or trading seats.
cons: Inability to effect change in the day to day of the desk and group you work in because of top-heavy setup.

advice: Allow your employees to take ownership of their work. Allow your employees to think like owners. No one there is a child and should be treated accordingly.
pros: Morgan Stanley is a good company and offers good benefits. Currently the company appears stable. Decent starting salary for those fresh out of college.
cons: Management lacks training. Environment seems childish. If management provided a better working environment employees may stay instead of consistently leave. High turn over rate in Baltimore Operations Center.

advice: Tell people exactly how the job will be during the interview process. Don't tell people they are guaranteed 18 months of production time, then let them go after 4 months!! I lasted 10 months but many others were gone within 3-4 months.
pros: Make your own schedule, no micro managing, they give you a senior advisor coach that can be helpful depending on who you get assigned, good for your resume.
cons: Lack of transparency with management, long hours for most people, you have to know people with money and be able to bring in 6 million pretty much right away for a realistic shot. Huge numbers you have to hit that ramp up quickly.

advice: I believe they are on the right track, Smith Barney is a large and complex effort 2012 will be a great year for MS
pros: There are alot of great managers here they make you feel welcome, the managers are trying to keep up with a large amount of change
cons: There are major budget constraints for 2012, the smith barney conversion is large effort and is taking alot of resources, once this migration is done there will be alot of resource bandwidth

summary: The culture has changed for the worse since Smith Barney became part of Morgan Stanley
advice: Pay attention to the field and their ask to service customer needs quickly and appropriately.
pros: Some really good talent still at the local level, comp is down the last 5+ years but still respectable.
cons: The firm has lost sight of its biggest asset in its customers and servicing them first. Adopting an old slogan of "we make our money the old fashion way, we earn it" would do a lot of good

summary: Experience was a complete function of manager and group
pros: This can be a pro or con: I worked in several groups in NY, and my experiences in terms of both professional growth and daily work satisfaction were very different depending on the group.
cons: Like I indicated above, it is very difficult through the interview process to get an adequate sense for the culture of the group of people with whom you would interact with on a daily basis.

advice: Create more paths for women with children. Senior women at that time had spent most of their careers at the office.
pros: I worked in the headquarters in NYC.  I loved the intellectual challenge of working with the brightest minds on Wall Street to create the best solution for the client.  Exceptionally nice group of people.  Pay for performance was excellent.
cons: While the company believes in employees having a work/life balance, the long hours makes this goal very difficult to achieve.

advice: Hold managers accountable to what they put in their emails. Make them indicate exactly what they want in writing.
pros: Some nice and talented people work there.
cons: Management considers giving clear instructions and any required technical information a huge burden to them. Asking any additional questions will get you into serious trouble so you have to guess what they want and beg people to help you get the required technical information. And even then, the projects might go disastrously wrong.

pros: You have tremendous autonomy which can be a good thing for the right person.  You can build your business any way you like and work as much or as little as you want granted you are generating business.  Huge firm with specialists for almost any financial need.
cons: The training does not sync up with the modern day challenges of a new, young financial advisor.  Goals are incredibly difficult unless you come into the program with guaranteed business.

pros: The individuals I work with are very knowladgable and are great people to work with in general. Major reason why I've stayed as long as I have.
cons: Micro-mangement of things that should not be. Incompetence of individuals who've been put in charge. I work in the Client Advisory Cener, which has great individuals whom are knowledgeable and try to help the client. The basis of how we are judged as an employee and actually trying to help the clients are NOT valued.

advice: Promote talent not seniority. Get rid of useless people. Make it easier for people to move and grow internally.
pros:
Great technology (in hindsight). I've moved on to other companies and technology is complete nightmare. I keep remembering ms apps with reverence, even though I thought it was bad when I worked there. 
A lot of good people. 
Ok career growth prospects, some chance to move around.
cons: New hiring situation at the time wasn't good and other people's jobs got rolled into yours.

summary: A good place to cut your teeth
pros: Large firm with a lot of resources to draw on if you know where to find it.  A brand that is respected around the world and opens a lot of doors.  Executive leadership is excellent, and was proud to work for James Gorman.
cons: Little support in training program which led to failure rate of program over 90%.  Seemed to be little trust/belief in people who had less than 15 years of experience in the industry.

advice: Encourage more candid feedback more regularly using the method that most consultant firms use because your employees want real advice consistently so they can grow
pros: Brand name will get you instant credibility wherever you go, clients are high profile so you usually get to work on the biggest deals with the most significant companies in the industry
cons: Hours are long although no longer than any other investment bank, pay is below Street because they can afford to given the brand name

advice: Management should be listening to the most junior people too, especially newcomers as they are the ones who have fresh opinion. General advise is to encourage skip-level manager sessions
pros: Firms indeed cares about its staff by offering various trainings, social events and other activities to keep work/life balance of the employees
cons: Depending on the department there is a strong corporate culture inside and it might not be flexible with proposed creative changes

advice: try to help new FAAs to grow their practices
pros: Great benefits, great staff, many advisors are genuinely looking to help.
cons: individualistic culture. One is not given any leads. One has to develop all business organically from nothing. So join only if you have natural network of at least 30mil for you to succeed after 3 years.

pros: You have the backing of an industry leading wealth management firm.   3 year decreasing base as you build your book.  You eat more if you get more
cons: The typical aches and pains of building book of business.  You only eat more if you get more

advice: Continue to invest in your people. Focus on leadership development, not just the bottom line.
pros: Great benefits, great culture. Lots of opportunities for advancement for ambitious, onboarding employees. Challenging work. Competitive environment, if you like those types of environments.
cons:
Volatile industry. Cut throat competition. Regularly told that "greed is good". No surprises here, most are very motivated by financial success but then again, this is Wall Street, right?

Once left for lunch and return to a quarter of the office having been laid off. Insane!

advice: Both academic research and real-life experience show that fewer better employees in IT can accomplish more than many lesser-quality employees. Outsourcing to lower cost on shore locations will yield higher productivity than to cheap off shore vendors.
pros: Top US bank. Leader in many areas. Especially strong in equities,  investment banking, and wealth management. Smart colleagues. Collegial environment
cons: The general business outlook is trending negative for the all large multinational banks. IT hiring does not pay competitively compared to top technology firms.

advice: Create a communtiy where the work life balance of the employees become over the average which will result higher engagement and improve on the quality as well.
pros: There are lot of opportunities to improve yourself in order to achieve better performance. You are also can get a promotion if you are enthusiastic and engaged to the company.
cons: In my humble opinion the work life balance not as good as i expected, just because there a good chance to do some work out of office hours.

pros: Multicultural environment, goal-oriented approach, relatively flat hierarchy and thus relatively promising promotional prospects, flexi hours many times, supportive to bring new ideas into existence.
cons: Weak focus on technical development more weight towards on soft skills, the starting salary looks attractive but later remains unindexed and getting less and less competitive over time, sometimes long hours but it is also an attribute of the sector.

advice:
Be nice to your employees. There is a famous phrase that people don't leave companies, they leave managers.
Try to own things, bring good technology work to India instead of just owning prod support work to build trust with global teams.
pros:
Good brand
Good compensation (joining salary + bonus)
cons:
Micro management
Bad work culture
Pushy environment.Rude managers
Hiring, firing culture
No freedom.
No work life balance
Mostly support work, less development work.Main development work happens in London and US.
Not good for Tech professionals
Ad hoc requirements come in between. Bad process

pros:
1. Good work-life balance. work from home is allowed in case of taking care of personal chore.
2. At least for my experience, most ppl I worked with are friendly.  A good reasonable boss make my life a lot easier.(which might note be the case for everyone)
cons:
It's not an engineer oriented environment. The engineering of development is rudimentary. Most of time, short term business goals decide everything. Long term architecture design is in second or least place.
Compensation is just around average of industry.

summary: Overall a good company to work
advice: Some of the managers need to be replaced especially those that have been in the same role for years. The need to transform to being leaders and not just managers, those in this category are usually not receptive to innovation or transformation. They talk the talk but won't allow their teams to be innovatively creative
pros: WorkLife balance, great salary, awesome coworkers
cons: HR needs to be more involved especially when employees complain about toxic managers or work environment

advice: Management did a solid job as far as I can tell and doesn't need my advice.
pros: Great company, friendly co workers and management. Decent pay, base plus commission was nice. Benefits were solid.
cons: Customers call in with the dumbest questions, and sometimes basically want you to justify their dumb investing moves, which we couldn't in good conscious do. Also sometimes people call in with their lawyers on the phone mad they lost money in the market, even though it was their own fault.

summary: Don't expect to get a big raise or promotion
advice: Tie raises to performance- not inflation. It's insulting. Encourage career growth instead of just hoping your top employees don't leave.
pros: Great learning experience. Big name for your resume. Benefits package is outstanding.
cons: What they say about never getting a raise is true. Being outstanding and having perfect performance reviews doesn't make one bit of difference. It's also too big of a company to have any space for creating solutions. Red tape everywhere.

summary: Only interested in the bottom line
advice: Look into ways to balance profits without sacrificing culture. You will get better results long term from employees who are not chronically exhausted.
pros: Morgan pays well, with great benefits and telecommuting options.  They encourage community service and outreach.  There are opportunities for travel and work overseas.
cons: There are routinely thousands of layoffs every year, which turns the work culture into an "every man for himself"environment.  Employees are unofficially expected to work 10-12 hour days on a regular basis.

summary: Demanding work culture with mixed gains
advice: Communicate more openly on things beyond earnings and highlight initiatives that are taken to better employee welfare since it has been a focus at other banks.
pros: Everyone is competent and works at a high level, and there are opportunities for advancement for those who commit.
cons: Company is resistant to evolving with the times and compensation increases lagged behind other banks for awhile in certain groups. Work life balance is difficult to maintain and no one makes serious attempts to better the situation.

advice: Need a TON more communication- managers who are recognized for certain awards and clubs don't treat "small people" with the respect they're preaching they give to everyone.
pros:
Core values
Philanthropy
Culture
Maternity leave
Health benefits
cons:
Not a ton of movement if you're not in new york

Disqualification from a position because of having a last minute cancellation with childcare and had to have my child home with me next to me. Never did interviewer ask if child care would be a problem just assumed I would be unavailable alot.

advice: Treat the temps and consultants a little better.  Give a little more notice so someone doesn't end up out of work as I did. I haven't been working in the industry since 2008.
pros: The employees were very willing to share their knowledge and experience with me. We all worked as a team for the most part.
cons: As a consultant with the firm, I was not told that the assignment was ending in time to find something else especially since they asked me to stay on permanently.

advice: Communicate more with staff regarding business changes, train regularly to support you staff in their career development, have career conversations quarterly or monthly.
pros: Ability to work independently if you are ambitious.
cons: Compensated horribly, good employees leave after 2-4 years because their compensation is very low and does not change significantly even with a promotion. Management never communicates with staff regarding helping business changes that occur yearly. Management does not perform career conversations with staff on a regular basis.

advice: please provide fairer treatment to less experienced advisers. please look into potentials and how to cultivate the pipeline rather than being results driven only.
pros: Brand name to win clients more easily. Entrepreneurial. unlimited and high quality research and client communications. access to top executives and client events to invite ultra high net worth clients.
cons: small payouts and bias towards senior advisers when resolving issues. very competitive training program. many restrictions for international business, but still better than competitor firms.

advice: I really do not have anything that could be of service here.  I have not been there long enough to have a very good opinion on what they could do better.
pros: I have a great opportunity to learn as from experienced professionals.  Very flexible with work and school.  Willing to help me out with recommendations and networking.
cons: I do not really do anything productive all day.  Since I started i have sorted through 50,000 letters that they have sent out and that is it.

advice: Offer the option of staying with the private bank if their is an opening.
pros: Private banking program was a great opportunity to become familiar with Morgan Stanley's lending services and also work with Financial Advisors.
cons: PBAA program had several flaws and the program had to be adjusted several times. At times the program posed issues with compliance because of the intermingling of lending a wealth management. Learning lending did not help much when it came to meeting the goals required of a financial advisor.

advice: keep up the good work, let people move up the ladder a bit more easily. give higher bonuses. its important to  recognize top performers.
pros: Work with smart people who want to learn and progress in their career. a great place to start. def. a place to consider
cons: very tough to move up the ladder. its more about who you know that what you know. take what you can from the job and take it elsewhere in your career

advice: I don't have a particular advice to give to my management at this point. I think a universal comment would be to have constant team communication so there is also clarity about what each team member is doing.
pros: Intelligent and interesting co-workers.  Many opportunities to learn. Great facilities and resources. Collegiate environment where most people are really open to share their knowledge.
cons: The one con I would like to mention would be that, as in most other investment banks, I have been working long hours.

advice: Management seems to cater to the larger producers and doesn't focus as much on those who are newer to the firm or don't produce as much revenue.
pros: The firm has hundreds of research analysts that produce in-house research on most investments. Good technology. Great work environment.
cons: They're still somewhat behind in becoming paperless. It seems like they make two steps forward (i.e. electronic signatures for A, B, and C), but one step back (i.e. you still need to sign for X,Y, and Z)

advice: Make decisions that are client focused, not firm focused.  The financial advisors own this firm, not the management.  You work for them.
pros: Global company with lots of opportunities.  Competitive environment with opportunities to excel and be rewarded.  Lateral and vertical movement available.
cons: Big and beaurocratic with uncertain job security in non-sales roles.  Upper management tends to micro manage.  The company is going through a difficult process of transformation and finding clear identity.

summary: Morgan Stanley is a place which values work life balance
advice: Reward staff and give them better compensation. Continue doing what you guys are doing, the culture is better than other places.
pros:
Morgan Stanley gives you a good brand name to kick start your career
It has one of the best if not the best working cultures and working hours you can ever find in banks
cons:
Compensation might not be as high as you expect it to be.
Long time to jump from one level to the next.

advice: Focus on long term solutions instead of short term fixes. Reevaluate hiring practices being a buddy does not guarantee job success and alienates the people in the trenches
pros: Morgan Stanley cache still carries weight in opening doors and soliciting new clients. Intellectual capital is significant and readily available.
cons: Management lacks specific direction to attain or complete designated goals. Cronyism rules the day and if you are not part of the clique expect to be trivialized and moved relocated.

summary: Morgan Stanley is one of the most unprofessional, non-structured chatic workplaces I've ever worked.
advice: Take sometime to learn about your business.  Decide which direction you want to go in - Global Wealth Mgmt or Underwriting and then spin off the other division.
pros: If you're an advisor with a large book of business and you want to get paid then this is the place for you.
cons: Complete lack of direction. The management, trainers and advisors are completely out of touch with no ability to teach someone how to be successful in the business.  They made it by cold calling in the 80's and don't have a clue how to build a business now.

advice: Look beyond Goldman and be less scared of Regulators
pros:
Good location
Open communication with Sr. Management
cons:
Too much work delegated to very few people. Some of the Sr. management seemed to not be interested in the work at all and just coasting through, while others were working really hard for inconsequential outcomes. Level of detail is one thing, but level of detail for reasons due to fear of regulators is not a recipe for success. 
Living in the shadows of Goldman and comparison to Goldman is too much.

summary: Overall, good place to work.  Limited opportunities for growth but good work/life balance.
pros: Overall, salary is around market.  Benefits are good but have been cut back in the last few years.  Work/life balance is really good.
cons: Limited opportunities for promotion or mobilitiy.  The company revolves around ibanking, so a bad year in ibanking will hurt other departments comp despite the individual groups performance.  Offices outside of NY are treated as secondary and often take a the brunt of cutbacks.

advice: get a clue.  We are people, not a number.  Stop trying to cut corners and cost.  You may look good to the big boss, but it sucks for us.
pros:
- somewhat flexible work schedule
- good benefits
- easy access to public transportation
- nice building
- HR is easy to talk to
- you don't bring your work home
cons:
- some people are not nice, they think they are gods
- cheap managers, microwave sucks, no milk for coffee
- they fire or lay you off, security walk you out immediately

advice: Keep up the quality of the people.
pros: Helpful and knowledgeable colleagues, flexible work hours, most of the IT managers also started as analysts, world-class technology background, nice, clean, roomy office, many office events organized, professional and soft-skills trainings, feels like a part of Wall Street moved to Budapest
cons: Sometimes too much bureaucracy is involved in the daily work, takes at least a year until a developer familiarizes himself with the business environment.

advice: A more formalized training program as well as structured learning experiences throughout the internship. The internship is a good starting point but is more useful for students in the earlier part of their college careers.
pros: Good starting internship. The people there are very nice and willing to help. Overall a good starting internship. Would recommend for sophomores.
cons: The pay is pretty low for a financial industry internship. The work is also exclusively grunt work. There is also no incentive for working faster or more efficiently.

summary: Good company culture with good people to execute it
advice: Ensure that the work life balance is propgated to the team in India. Most of the time it is assumed that India team will not see their evenings
pros:
1) Lead the team from India and own the project.
2) Directly talk with the business to get requirements and drive yourself
3) Excellent work
4) Working with world-class infrastructure
cons: 1) Work life balance is little sqewed. The person needs to learn to say no.

summary: Operations is for those with little drive
advice: Do not promise things you cannot carry through on.  Employees should be treated better than you treat yourself, because they can move faster than you could bat an eye
pros: Work is at a minimum. operations areas are an easy paycheck, but people get too comfortable and do the minimum.  Its a comfortable job.
cons: Complete waste of time.  If you want to switch to any type of front office position good luck.  Half the skills you learn are a complete throw away.

summary: Pay getting worse, increasing outsourcing both on- and offshore.
advice: Realize that Gorman is perceived as a jerk in the lower ranks, and it depresses morale. Paying millions to traders and for the others it's "if you're unhappy, just leave".
pros: Very flexible work arrangements, good technology stack (on the Morgan side, the SB side works with vacuum tubes)
cons: Zero bonus for years now, LOTS of H1B- staff and India teams which depresses comp for everyone (local leaves->3 new India hires), really cool tasks (mobile, etc.) outsourced to contractors.

summary: Great meritocratic environment, but with significant churn
advice: Keep up the communication!  Morgan Stanley employees are skilled at change, but uncertainty creates confusion and insecurity.
pros: If you find the right group and management, Morgan Stanley is a true meritocracy -- employees are appreciated and recognized for good work and ingenuity.
cons: Be prepared for change -- constant change.  Back office employees change managers, buildings, and organizations on a recurring basis.  As well, the industry is doing a "musical chairs" exercise right now, so departures and new hires are frequent.

summary: Great place to work most of the time.
advice: The constant amount of attrition that goes on does not make for a stable environment. It also leads to loss of valued employees.
pros: Great NYC locations. Great people. Great pay and benefits. Great training options. Great Employee Relations. Ability to work remote from home.
cons: The biggest con is the feeling around the agency when impending layoffs are constantly being announced or rumored. No one feels safe or certain how long they will last, from Management on down.

summary: Balanced work/life but not enough intellectual satisfaction
advice: There should be smother way of people to explore other options within the firm. Switcing teams is sometimes a tough job and not all EDs appreciate the significance. Some even deny outright
pros:
There are many pros:
Very smart colleagues, open doors, many forums to share knowledge, good people, good work/ life balance, good benefits,
cons: I personally felt there was a lack of intellectual satisfaction for me. Not much challenges to take and be proud of. Did not feel I was learning enough on the job

advice: Morgan Stanley needs to provide better training to managers, back office and support staff. Conferences for support staff (like those offered to financial advisors)would offer opportunity for professional development and to share best practices.
pros: Salary is competitive.  Management shows appreciation for the support staff.
cons: Client Service Managers are not given the training necessary to be a reliable technical and practical resource for the client service associates. Rotation among the office branches of these CSM's occurs regularly for some reason, causing constant disruption.

summary: Great place to go, not start
advice: You've got the training backwards.
pros: The best fixed income desk in the business. Syndicate is fantastic if you have the production and client base to get access to any new issues. You're in the center of the world.
cons: Terrible pay and benefits. No expense accounts. All the marketing, sales development, and lead sources are paid by the trainee. Unless you are on a team you get no marketing support. Training is almost non-existent. I had a great complex but unfortunately they were over worked and understaffed.

advice: Understand the wants and needs of your employees and allow them the oppotunity to shine. Also, provide the right level of advancement or people will leave.
pros: Great People and Great Benefits. I learned a great deal of information and was able to take advantage of the excellent benefits!
cons: In certain departments there are few opportunities for advancement. Additionally they make no effort to offer employment mobility to other areas of the firm.

advice: Appreciate your employees, treat them as people- not worker bees.
pros: I personally think it's a decent place to start off- despite the fact that the skills  and knowledge you accumulate aren't very pertinent to much else. I think as an intern, you learn more about the soft-skills which is important. I would not stay here and here and expect much of a career
cons:
-Seems like only horizontal progressions
-criteria for promotion/progression is vague and inconsistent. 
- Culture is paper thin, and constantly shifting and readjusting

summary: I enjoy working at Morgan Stanley
advice: It would be nice to have a career development plan that extends beyond a few years.
pros:
- supportive and friendly teams and atmosphere
- interesting day-to-day tasks that support professional development
- exposure to other cultures and nationalities
- flexible management so long as you do a proper job
cons:
- limited development and promotion opportunities, no long-term career development opportunities as the place of business is located elsewhere
- bureaucracy and countless policies 
- sometimes too many meetings and other multinational activities take up your whole working day

summary: Good Infrastructure, good software development opportunities, bad salaries
pros:
1. Good Infrastructure
2. You will get to learn many things in technology in the initial years(but it gets kind of plain and boring after that.)
3. Chance of making good friends
cons:
1. Ineffective strategies by senior management.
2. Work Culture is becoming more and more political
3. Salaries don't go up according to the hard work you put in, because it is driven by the business, which is heading south, and not by IT

advice: Find new, innovative ways to compensate and engage employees so your offices are no longer known for being revolving doors.
pros: Strong, stable organization with a prominent name in the financial services industry.
cons: Zero opportunities for career advancement. They changed their sales staff compensation 4 times in 5 years; it was annoying. I was once told a program and position I was hired for was no longer being offered at the firm via email. In a firm this large, you are easily replaced.

summary: great culture, great pay but the good times are ending
pros: You will work with the most distinguished crew of professionals in the industry, great culture and extremely good exposure to top level opportunities, pay and benefits are top of the line as well.
cons: Gorman's drive to purge the investment banking and trading business means the good days are gone and all the pros mentioned above will no longer be offered to new comers, attrition rates are alarmingly high this year.

advice: Try and take the time to get to know what will keep your employees in house, increase the intangible benefits and create an open and collaborative environment with senior management
pros: Advanced my knowledge in the finance services industry and operations as a whole as well as providing the support to hone in on project management excellence and skills.
cons: Growth and Salary i would consider a couple of cons within the part of the organization i am a part of.

advice:
More team to team integration/encouraging associates to move beyond their pod
Mid-summer performance reviews should be more candid/direct about areas to improve
pros:
Great crash course into the life of an associate
Lots of senior speaker events, networking events, etc.
Given lots of responsibility
cons:
Seniors are not incredibly approachable (usually have to book time with your Analyst)
Greuling presentation/stock pitch at the end of internship ( be overprepard, very important)
Training program is brief
Not always clear what you're looking for in terms of the projects given to you

advice: Allow more work flexibility. With technology, it's not always necessary to be chained to a desk. Flexible work arrangements would attract younger talent.
pros: Morgan Stanley is an excellent company for me to jump start my career. I had incredible support from my managers and colleagues who were genuinely interested in my personal and professional growth.
cons: Though my direct managers were a blessing, there was inevitable politics that would spill over into my role as is expected working in such a large organization.

advice: Morgan Stanley is a very good place for a balanced work life fun place to go every day again and again. Excellent vision mission and directions
pros: Morgan Stanley is a very good place for a balanced work life fun place to go every day again and again.
cons: Morgan Stanley is a very good place for a balanced work life fun place to go every day again and again. Each and every day is a challenge to keep you charged and motivated and focused. not for short term career  seekers.

summary: Over worked, Under appreciated, Very Chaotic work environment
advice: Start caring more about employees. They lose talent because they are only numbers driven.
pros: Benefits package was decent. 401k match is great.
cons: They showed appreciation by giving you more to do. Management was very disorganized. Low moral among employees. They couldn't even cater company parties... they were potlucks. Unless you use your insurance often it is expensive. Not an open environment for suggestions to improve. If suggestions are given they are never acted on.

summary: Acquisition of Smith Barney not going smoothly
advice: Need to staff up in certain areas.  Management needs to communicate much better to employees, and needs to keep them updated - whether the news is good or bad.
pros: Industry leader in many aspects, well respected firm.   Sound reputation, great opportunities to learn.  Team atmosphere, co workers were very helpful.
cons: Profits not coming quickly enough.  Firm not expanding, no new employees in years, staff that has survived cutbacks is very demoralized.

advice: Put yourself in your employees place and try to treat people how you want to be treated, try to find jobs within the company for you employees before you just send them out after working for you for more than 10, 20, or 30 years.
pros: To gain knowledge with job function and cross training. The co workers that I worked with.
cons: These corporations will lay you off know matter how much of your time that you have dedicated to them.

summary: i can learn a lot in Morgan Stanley
advice: it would be better if manager can provide team building, give more drinks and food. pay more attention to the work load balance.
pros: can learn lots of finance knowledge, and the compensation is good.  there is a lot of opportunity to learn finance knowledge.
cons: need ware formal cloth, which is a little harder for a IT tech. build environment is bad. the release cycle is too short and workload balance is not satisfied.

advice: Focus on what is really right for the client rather than just production. Possibly provide some incentive regarding client longevity.
pros: Excellent research, trading, product offerings. Ability to work mobile at times. I had an excellent manager and a nice small office.
cons: No middle tier jobs. Sales Assistant or Financial Advisor. Would love to see a position on a team that includes younger employees and those wishing to reduce their goals, but still want to be an asset to the team.

summary: Great place to work if you like repetitive tasks
pros: The compensation was good enough to work through the drudgery of the job that I had. The people were overall nice, but you never knew who would stab you in the back.
cons: You can easily get into a groove where you are doing the same thing over and over again. Don't get stuck doing repetitive tasks! My job was on the border of being offshored, but it required a good handle on the English language.

advice: Reward loyal employees, train them and promote them to leadership instead of hiring leadership from outside.
pros: MS is still recognized as a top employer brand on the job market, which gives an advantage in the CV.
cons:
Total reward is BS. The company takes financial advantage of loyal employees meanwhile spending large amounts hiring senior positions and consultants.

Over the years, it is becoming a more bureaucratic, red tape organization.

advice: the training program should be seriously revamped if you expect to cultivate the next era of financial advisors.
pros: Great benefits, competitive environment that fostered a community approach.  It also felt like they were working hard to bring firm into the new millennium by introducing advanced technology.
cons: terrible training and unrealistic sales expectations - unless you have a built in clientele or you wind up in a partnership, the chance of succeeding as a financial advisor becomes difficult.

advice: Reward and take extra care of your most valued employees, so that you do not lose them to your competitors.  Find a way!
pros: Advancement Opportunities, Work/Life Balance, Top Benefits including Flexible work schedule, work from home, 4 weeks paid vacation, opportunity to transfer, etc.
cons: Salary could be more competitive with peers, especially for employees that have been with the firm for a long time.

advice: Pay your employees more based on the good work they do and recognize them more both during the year and at year end.  Pay based on performance!!
pros: Great area to learn a lot and gain knowledge and help in customer service.  Work hours are ok and employees are willing to help each other
cons: Pay is not good and there is no work/life balance.  Employees are not recognized for hard work at year end.  Morale is low

summary: Work in Morgan Stanley is rewarding
advice: For the research franchise, it is better to implement the incentive policy on the quality of research. After all, it is the core competitativeness for sales and trading business.
pros: MS has a great platform to improve personal capability. Diversified culture attract talents from all of world, and compensation is highly competitative.
cons: Leadership in specific area, e.g., research, needs more time to test. The evaluation system does not value the quality of research.

pros: Stability, huge size, a lot of technology is present, you can learn almost about anything in the company. The mentality and the culture of the firm can be felt, people are very helpful, not only from the local office, but also from other offices as well.
cons: Huge size, large hierarchies, sometimes its hard to achieve the smallest thing. There can be cases, depending on the teams, when you get to do repetitive job for a very long period.

advice: Keep doing good work and keep making their employees happy, we will happily grow with the company. Also if they can negotiate a better health plan with the providers, they will become "good to great".
pros: The firm respects diversity. The people here are professional and friendly. Lots of training available for free if you're up for it. They also promote remote computing and volunteering for charities.
cons: The medical insurance they provide only covers 80% after you meet your deductible.

advice: it depends on team to team. some team managers seriously think about their teams and some not.
pros: Good working environment and lot to learn for a new joiner. you can specialize on most of the trading aspects from the infrastructure point of view. Work life balance is good.
cons: Its difficult to grow in ladder because there is a long queue and specially if you don't have any one backing you from senior management. growth become stuck at mid senior level.

summary: Great culture but doesn't pay enough
advice: Stop moving key jobs over to other remote locations
pros:
- Great culture and the people they hire are extremely hard working, intelligent and easy to work with
- Promotes mobility
- Training courses are available everywhere
- Encourages meeting others from different departments
cons:
- For the amount of hours and stress we put in/receive, they do not pay their employees well
- Training courses are available but there's no time to delve into a course you're into

advice: Investment banking as a whole needs a revamp. The crippling attention to detail and the disregard for the lives and balance of their employees is stale. This isn't a MS problem, it's across the board.
pros: The highest caliber of professionalism  (at the senior level)
cons: At the junior level, professionalism is lacking. Attacks on my character, inappropriate questions, uncomfortable comments have continually been made to me.  Higher management doesn't always care to respect your time (industry wide issue)

summary: Good company to your start career
pros:
-employees are not stuffy or overly pretentious as in other banks
-intelligent and personable colleagues
-great benefits and access to a lot of discounts around major cities
-highly regarded firm amongst the industry
-the firm is working on being more innovative and trying to attract young talent (which is an overall problem for the entire Finance industry vs. tech)
cons:
-bureaucratic /political
-promotions depend heavily on division/manager; not very clear on the career mobility timeline

advice: Fix your documentations and procedures. Respect time of employees
pros:
Great external reputation
Nice to have on a resume
Above average pay
cons:
Training material scattered over numerous intranet sites - excruciating to find information that seem trivial in other companies
Technology stack is old and "Morganized" so extra learning curve paired with tedious SDLC processes
Must learn new tech outside of work if you want to remain marketable
Zero work life balance with no culture of overtime pay - don't join if you actually like your spouse and kids.

summary: A good name but not much to back it up.
advice: Offer employees a hybrid work environment and more flexible hours where coverage is available.
pros: Morgan Stanley is a strong, prestigious company. theyve provided a lot of recent investment in technology which is great. I feel secure in my job
cons: Difficult to move up in the wealth management field. Little to no perks. Felt extremely unsupported throughout the pandemic and coming back from maternity leave. Annual raises are extremely minimal. Lots of red tape to get anything accomplished.

pros:
High quality people - very smart, hard-working, but also generally nice as well
Collaborative culture that values intellectual curiosity 
Strong leadership
Good benefits
cons:
Up or out work environment
Like all banks when there are downturns layoffs happen and some very talented people end up leaving because they were in the wrong role at the wrong time
Like all banks work life balance can be a challenge

advice: Work with your employees on salary arrangements. The promotion/raise timeline is too stringent. Should be on a case by case basis
pros: Nice to work for a large corporation. Good team environment.
cons: Severely underpaid for the amount of work you’re expected to do. The turnover for the analyst positions out of Baltimore is astronomical. They want to “retain talent” but at the end of the day it’s cheaper to higher fresh out of college kids than to give salary raises to employees when they deserve it.

summary: The company does not care about your health
advice: Please be responsible for your employees and the society.
pros: There are definitely many pros here.
cons: The company "suggests" people to come back to the office during the covid even when omicron is spreading. On top of that, some teams within the firm were hosting official parties in person. A large number of people who went to those parties got covid and kept spreading the virus to other people, including their families and their loved ones.

advice: Increase the salary for support staff.  Advisors are willing to step all over the support staff to increase their salaries with little to no reward for the people working for them.
pros: Great position to learn the business & grow towards being a financial advisor
cons: It's all about the advisor you work for. If you are on a team with a great advisor the job will be rewarding and fun, if not, it will be difficult. Advisors typically have strong personalities.

summary: Nice company but promotion can take years
advice: YOu talk the good talk but you don't really plan for your people's careers.
pros: Nice people. Clear goals. Interesting work. No weekend work which is nice. Very fair during pandemic.
cons: Make sure you come in at a level that you will be happy with for some time. Promotions only happen once a year and you cannot try for a job internally that's at a different level than what you're at. Social mobility is only easy at the very low levels.

summary: Great Company, but department could use improvement
advice: Training needs to be completely overhauled, many colleagues admitted to not being prepared to go into the role. Once you are out of the training phase, there is very limited support to ensure that you are following correct procedures.
pros:
Benefits are very fair
Company technology is advanced yet easily accessible.
Cutting edge market research
cons:
Training was inadequate. Position was very trial by fire oriented.
No flexibility in terms of working remotely once you are in the office
Pay was underwhelming

advice: Pay us more. And pay us equally. If the market price for a position goes up, compensate the current employees at the same rate that the new employees are being hired at. Make hybrid schedules optional, there's literally 0 need to return to the office unless we want to. Company is suffering major turnover due to these two things... What's not connecting???
pros: Great teammates and colleagues (depending on what part of the business you're working in
cons:
Pay... PAY... P A Y!
Forced hybrid/in-office schedules

advice:
Mind the overtime burden and accept the fact that that overtime work affects the psychology of workers
Respect time zone differences
pros: Quite a diverse and internationally known investment firm where you will learn something new and make a good professional network
cons: Working with different time zones may be difficult in the sense that sometimes the other stakeholder pushes you to finish the job and then leave the office even if it is out-of-working hours.

summary: Enjoy the money but you live at work.
advice: Teach the managers leadership skills.  Promotions should be based on contributions to the firm more than kissing up to the boss.  Managers should learn to share more and not create fiefdoms.
pros: The money is what draws you in.  There is also the corporate name for your resume and to most people it is a highly respected name.
cons: The long hours.  Promotion based on time in a group and are you buddies with the boss.

advice: Management needs to focus on the professional development of its enormous salesforce, on increasing the product knowledge of its salesforce and most of all needs to ensure that client objectives are the number one priority
pros:
Reputation and Client Base
Compensation and Benefits
The research was top notch and the firm was involved in major deals
cons: The sheer magnitude of the salesforce was overwhelming - there appeared to be a focus on quantity, not quality, which led to an unusually high rate of attrition

advice: Overall you are making the firm better.  However,by pushing out those that produce under $400,000, you are reducing the number of big producers you will have in the future.
pros: Unlimited income potential, control your own schedule, challenging work, competitive environment, run your business like an entrepeneur, help clients achieve their goals
cons: There is no guaranteed salary.  If you are not bringing in enough business, you will have to find a new job.

advice: I could not be happier with the leadership of the firm.  Top notch people are in this industry and it is apparent from the top down why.
pros: The ultimate opportunity to create your own destiny and have no limit as to how much you will work and how much you will earn!
cons: You had better be extrememly self motivating.  Nobody really cares what you do, because you are building your own business and the proof is in the pudding.

advice: Give more people the ability to have their cake and eat it too. In other words, give them real exposure to problems and allowed them to achieve results that can be put on resumes.
pros: Great mentors who will share their investment wisdom with you and teach you the ropes while giving you substantial work during the experience.
cons: Not a lot to put on your resume. Mainly stock research and interacting with clients. Hard to quantify achievements or list technical skills.

summary: Internship at Morgan Stanley Smith Barney
advice: Make some entry level jobs available to college graduates who had an internship with the company.  Also possibly offer paid internships.
pros: The internship was great.  I learned a lot about private wealth management and it was a great experience to put on my resume.  Not much available for full-time job afterwards.
cons: There was no availability for a full time job placement after my internship.  Many of the interns were also unpaid.

advice: I don't think they would read anything from here if they cant read from there employees inside.
pros: Pay is good. Some of the facilities are also good like transport to home etc.
cons:
Work life balance is really bad. 
Promotion criteria is different for fresh hires and laterals. Dont keep high hopes if you join below VP.
I Don't think they need senior application developers in India.
More of a change shop rather and support call center.

summary: No loyalty, well below market compensation
advice:
Be honest with your employees.

Try to keep the compensation of long time employees in line with market rates.
pros:
Hours in this particular group are very decent but this fluctuates based on the time of year and the group.

Relatively patient work environment.
cons: Comp is extremely low especially for long time employees. The firm has no sense of loyalty to  their employees and it shows in the way management treats employees from both a compensation and work life balance.

advice: Really push the employees to take the next step in getting their series 7, the desk is the perfect launching pad for it.
pros: Easy hours, laid back environment, the teams really work together, the work is not difficult easy launching pad for anyone looking to get some insight into the stock market without getting too close
cons: This particular role is run like a call center so you are essentially chained to your desk the majority of the day.

advice: convert people to full time. Ive seen coworkers go 5 years as consultants, and finally get ocnverted, and only because someone left.
pros: Decent pay, comparable to full time. Good experience and exposure to corporate environment. Days go fast because there's too much to do.
cons: Consultants can be laid off at any time. Do the same amount of work as full timers and put in the same amount of hours but not recognized for it. No bonus and mandatory furlough to save the firm even more money.

pros:
Compensation , Brand Value , Work from home , Year end bonus , training, open door policy in real.
Good company, provided its not technology that drives you.
cons:
Its not a technology company, that's what you will here once you are in.its a investment bank want to see final numbers no matter how you use the technology.
Junk processes and junk or monotonous work.
late evening calls on daily basis, long working hours irrespective real work , weekend turnovers.

advice: Appreciate the value of those reporting to you. Don't mix the boundary between developer and quantitative analyst.
pros: The opportunity to work with smartest people in the industry, and launch a great career. You can learn a lot from people around you. People are all very approachable. I don't know anyone that would act like an axxhole here.
cons: The red tape. Your value isn't much appreciated. I feel that many of my colleagues are undervalued in this environment. They deserve to stay in a better company.

advice: Do not just fill spots with people you like if they do not fit the job description.  The hiring/placement process for interns could be improved a lot.
pros: Good compensation for the amount of work you have to do
cons: Work itself is not very engaging.  They try to force you into positions where they think they see you fit regardless of what your background sets you up well for (i.e. women are forced into sales roles, while men go into trading)

advice: There is a major problem when the CEO's and officers get multimillion dollar bonuses and the average worker gets barely a 1% raise each year. The company is full of intelligent women and men who create the products that generate the revenue. It is disheartening to see the fruits of our labor so unequally divided.
pros:
Company culture of learning and integrity
Strong leadership
cons:
Low compensation
Bureaucracy
Disparity between compensation for senior officers and all other employees

summary: Overall a good company to work for but disappointed in treatment of lower level employees.
advice: Be more transparent. Treat your team like a team and have everyone on the same page. Stop playing favorites.
pros:
Benefits- 4 months off paid maternity leave.
Work life balance- only require you to work 9 HR days. Limited over time. Flexible when needing time off.
cons: Management is very reactive instead of proactive. A lot of unneeded stress and work is created due to lack of communication. Corporate politics play a huge factor everyday.

advice: Treat all staff with respect and realize your role is to be a  support to Staff & FA’s
pros: The benefit / medical  Package is amazing
cons: Operations support in Branch and back office are useless and do not want to help nor do they know how to help . If your not with the in crowed you will feel like an outcast and they will ignore you and blame you for everything even if it’s failure to supervise.

summary: A pretty good place to start your career at.
advice: The firm could be more robust in bringing in new technologies to the firm, to be up-do-date with the current world.
pros:
Provides good compensation
Great work ethics and high standards
Awesome co-workers & atmosphere altogether
Plenty of social events and opportunities to initiate one
cons:
Business casual dress-code even in the back office.
You can't always work with the latest technology in the enterprise environment.
Can be overly PC in some cases, especially for people not used to working at Banks.

summary: Amazing firm in every way, hampered by attrition due to lack of willingness to compensate top young talent.
pros: Phenomenal senior management with vision and innovation. The firm really does seem to hold true to its five pillars of business as opposed to just using them as punchlines.
cons: Sluggish promotion process and lack of compensation for top young talent. Far to many individuals leave in search of better salaries that the firm is not willing to provide.

advice: Look to help people and actually further their careers. Discuss with FA's what they're looking for rather than having consultants drive what's most important.
pros: There is unlimited upside potential and the firm puts a lot of resources back into the company and specifically wealth management. You can earn as much as your able to bring in.
cons: You eat what you kill. If you don't bring in assets that create revenue, you don't make any money. Quick to dismiss if you're not keeping up.

advice: Wake up, you are losing in good people and in reputation.
pros: Just the benefits, little better than the general market
cons: This company has a very arrogant and cruel HR department. They only care about protecting the company. Every real issue that is brought to them is dismissed and with a revenge. If you are thinking about raising a complain, don't bother. They will just make your life miserable.

advice: Focus more on the analyst and associates that show they want to do their best and contribute to the firms overall goals and help you achieve yours. They might surprise you and help you along your way up the chain also.
pros: Work life balance is by far the key to what has separated them from my past employers.
cons: Haven't found that my management truly cares about my career development and advancement. Upper management is super cliche and really only push their own agendas.

advice: Create an ad for an internship that is truthful for what it is. A cold calling job. I would not consider this to be an internship as I learned nothing.
pros:
The majority of the people were nice.
It is a good professional environment.
cons:
Not what the ad for the internship described.
All I did was cold call prospects for 2 financial advisors 3 hours a day for 3 days a week. 
There wasn't any learning of the business other than cold calling.

advice: Pay people their worth or else turnover will continue at the rate it is. a buy side firm offered me a 50% raise and I took it even though I liked my job at MSFS.
pros: I had great managers who listened and cared about work/life balance.
cons: Salary was way below market value, base only went up $1k one year. Senior management at fund services is too old school, lots of turnover, no visibility to other parts of the firm

advice: Stop thinking that "year of experience" or "years at Morgan Stanley" shows how valuable an employee is. In fact people that have stayed at the company for a long time lack original ideas and abuse their power through politics. There is no consequence for not delivering. Start measuring KPIs and OKRs and hold leadership accountable. The lack of accountability is baffling.
pros: Good Gym, Good Cafeteria, Nice Mailroom
cons: Bad Leadership , Bad Culture, Low Pay, Negative Staff, No Concept of Team, Team Members Put Each Other Down, Leadership Sets a Bad Example, Rotten People, Slackers, People that Dont Have Expertise, Low Level Of Skill, Not Motivating, List Can go On and On

advice:
Make the employee salary's transparent.
Promote from within instead of hiring out. Pay your minority employees the same as your white male employees.
pros: If you are in a good group, you will have a good experience with work life balance.
cons: You have to play the networking game to advance. For real. Working hard and being good at what you do, doesn't advance you. Your friends in high places advance you.

summary: Group specific - but when group culture is bad, not even HR has your back.
advice: HR needs to have less ties to senior leaders and be empowered to support individual team members.
pros: Great career recognition, and good responsibilities. If your team is in a good part of the business, MS is one of the best places to work. Definitely forward looking in a lot of their businesses.
cons: If you have a bad manager who is tied to someone with clout, there are no repercussions.

summary: Good Culture, needs better leaders and better pay
pros: Great culture and opportunities to network.
cons:
It's clear that their standards for promotion are not the same for everyone. I got a promotion but it was clear the extra work I had to do to get a promotion that someone else got only because they have been with the firm for a while and not based on any other merit. 
They also underpay us in comparison to other salaries in the industry

summary: Morgan Stanley - Nirvana for technical people on Wall Street

advice: You haven't planted one foot solidly before taking the next step in years now. pros: Co workers are generally pleasant to work with
cons: Toxic behaviour is tolerated by management if you are in their good graces.

advice: Get rid of the people who are giving a half baked effort.  Promote from within more often than hiring externally.
pros: In IT, there is flexibility for women (and men) to work from home.  The culture is a bit more laid back than some of the other IBs I've worked for.  People enjoy working collaboratively and like to share ideas.
cons: There needs to be stronger leadership.  Decision making by way of consensus is not the best approach

advice: Within 5-10 years the average financial advisor will be 60-70 years old and you will need to have younger advisors - begin to integrate them into your overall practice.
pros: Top of the line research and market insight

advice: Talents are important in every organization. I think its important to pay the market rate particularly for performing individuals.

summary: Not a great place to work if you looking for work life balance

summary: Great Culture and a lovely organization to work for

cons: Some of the the downsides was that there was not much praise for actually completing tasks. It was more of just a do what you want type deal.

summary: large company way behind in technology

advice: No useless work.  More flexibility in taking time off.  Less stuffy work environment.  Doesn't make sense how uppity the environment is.

summary: Cost cutting taken to the extreme
advice: Cost cutting focus has had a positive impact on the bottom line but at the expense of employee morale. pros: Strong firm with good outlook, good compensation (at least for those 'in the club'), great talent.

advice: Focus on former employee engagement; large consulting firms do this much better than banks, it seems.
pros: Morgan Stanley's investment banking division rewards top talent and focuses on the development of its people. It's hard not to learn a lot.
cons: Work-life balance was poor; the culture of overwork came from the top, and resulted in burnout for many analysts. It seems that Goldman Sachs has led in this area in trying to make improvements -- hopefully Morgan Stanley will follow.

summary: You learned a great depth of knowledge and gain tons of product sales skills

cons: Not to much of a team atmosphere as advisors are mainly working by themselves to find clients and maintain their relationships with them.

advice: keep up the good work and keep promoting the Morgan Stanley culture as that is what has kept me there until today.

cons: currently my only concern is they are not located close to where i live and so i have to drive an hour and a half one way to get to the office.

cons: Recent breaking of the linkage between performance and pay, and a constant changing in strategy for the fixed income businesses leaves some employees stranded.

advice: Keep up the good work.

advice: More money should be spent on employees to keep them motivated and on target to reach deadlines. Additional emlpoyees may be needed in certain groups.

Prefer band aids rather than longer term solutions.

advice: Definitely a great place to start your career, lots of networking opportunities as I mentioned before, and having Morgan Stanley on your resume can do some wonders.

advice: Overall a great experience.  I would suggest Senior teams visit the regional offices more often to communicate strategic direction in a clearer format.
pros:

encouraged us to constantly learn and take classes, seminars

summary: Overall, it is a great firm to work for..

cons: Changes are made quite too frequently. Although frequent policy changes bring ramifications, it is clear that those changes are being made in an effort to promote the work environment and betterment. Also, with the process of joint venture, it is somewhat inevitable.

advice:
Mumbai Tech & Data division has ineffective Managing Directors & Executive Directors which makes the office full of politics. In the name of local management they are fooling NY management. They provide no technical help, they don't have any accountability but have full authority over Mumbai employee's career growth.....what a pity!

My advice to management is......take a look at other investment banks in India and see how good they are doing, and learn from them.
pros:
I worked for Morgan Stanley Mumbai, Tech & Data division (Software development) for few years. For first 3-4 years it was a great place to work. There was a focus on technology solutions for the business. People were ethical and genuinely wanted to make a difference. Work environment was open. Also, Firm was doing good on revenue & profits. But after that, due to bad policy decisions
and weak leadership hiring, good and talented people from business side and IT side started leaving the firm and the situation deteriorated.

I do not see any reason for a talented professional to work at Morgan Stanley now.  If you really don't care about your learning and only want to be lured of some percentage of hike, then only join Morgan Stanley.
cons:
Even in Software development divisions, middle & senior management is non technical or out of technical touch. Their only focus is to keep their jobs by politics or otherwise. Firm is New York focused and teams in Mumbai office are mere daily wage kind of labor for them. Very poor facilities to employees as compared to other investment banks & software cos. in India, be it salary structure, cafeteria, transportation or anything else.

Annual performance reviews and ratings are not transparent.

cons: Not much support for starting up. You are really on your own and must be a very high performer to meet the monthly requirements. IF you can make it, it is the best job in the world.

pros: Banking firm with a technology attitude - great people to work with and more importantly, learn from. Work-life balance is excellent, and technology really is top-notch.
cons: No major cons, some politics but generally you get to do your work in peace

advice: pay better, offer better assistance for mobility outside of operations if someone has the desire to move to the front office, more consistency within group so workload is spread out better
pros: Exposure to institutional side of financial markets and trading, young workforce, team camaraderie, new office, great location on water
cons: Compensation, lack of bonus, lack of feedback from managers, higher performers aren't valued as well as they could be, very political climbing the corporate ladder, lack of mobility outside of operations

pros: ppl around you are general experienced and quite professional. benefit in general on par within the industry. it requires self discipline a lot of time if you have a remote manager.
